lehigh-2020-02.title: Spot the right angle
lehigh-2020-02.body:
$16^2+30^2=256+900=1156=34^2$, so the triangle is right with legs $16$ and $30$. Area $=\frac12\cdot16\cdot30=240$.

**Answer: 240**

lehigh-2020-03.title: Set up the vinegar balance
lehigh-2020-03.body:
Let $x$ liters of the $20\%$ solution be added. Vinegar: $0.2x+0.5\cdot4=0.3(x+4)$, so $0.1x=0.8$ and $x=8$.

**Answer: 8 liters**

lehigh-2020-03.title: Weighted average
lehigh-2020-03.body:
The target $30\%$ is $20$ points below $50\%$ and $10$ points above $20\%$. So the amounts are in ratio $20\%:50\%$ solution $=2:1$. With $4$ liters of the $50\%$ solution we need $8$ liters of the $20\%$ solution.

**Answer: 8 liters**

lehigh-2020-04.title: Add rates
lehigh-2020-04.body:
In minutes, Alex paints $\frac1{180}$ of the room per minute and together they paint $\frac1{72}$. Chris's rate is $\frac1{72}-\frac1{180}=\frac{5-2}{360}=\frac1{120}$, so Chris needs $120$ minutes.

**Answer: 120 minutes**

lehigh-2020-04.title: Compare work done in 72 minutes
lehigh-2020-04.body:
In $72$ minutes Alex does $\frac{72}{180}=\frac25$ of the room, so Chris does $\frac35$. Therefore the whole room takes Chris $72\cdot\frac53=120$ minutes.

**Answer: 120 minutes**

lehigh-2020-05.title: Weekday shift per leap day
lehigh-2020-05.body:
Between consecutive leap days there are $4\cdot365+1=1461=7\cdot208+5$ days, so the weekday of February 29 advances by $5$ every $4$ years (no century year occurs before 2100). February 29, 2020 was a Saturday. We need $5k\equiv0\pmod 7$, so $k=7$ steps, i.e. $28$ years: $2020+28=2048$.

**Answer: 2048**

lehigh-2020-05.title: List the weekdays
lehigh-2020-05.body:
Feb 29 after the Saturday of 2020: 2024 Thursday, 2028 Tuesday, 2032 Sunday, 2036 Friday, 2040 Wednesday, 2044 Monday, 2048 Saturday.

**Answer: 2048**

lehigh-2020-06.title: Two equations
lehigh-2020-06.body:
Let $G$ students wear glasses out of $T$. Then $\frac{G+1}{T+1}=\frac14$ gives $T=4G+3$, and $\frac{G-1}{T-1}=\frac15$ gives $T=5G-4$. So $4G+3=5G-4$, $G=7$, $T=31$. Check: $\frac8{32}=\frac14$ and $\frac6{30}=\frac15$.

**Answer: 31**

lehigh-2020-07.title: Use the discriminant
lehigh-2020-07.body:
The roots are $\frac{-p\pm\sqrt{p^2-4}}2$, which differ by $\sqrt{p^2-4}$. So $\sqrt{p^2-4}=1$, $p^2=5$, and $p=\sqrt5$ since $p>0$.

**Answer: $\sqrt5$**

lehigh-2020-07.title: Vieta
lehigh-2020-07.body:
Let the roots be $r$ and $r+1$. Then $r(r+1)=1$ and $2r+1=-p$. From the first, $(2r+1)^2=4r^2+4r+1=5$, so $p^2=5$ and $p=\sqrt5$.

**Answer: $\sqrt5$**

lehigh-2020-08.title: Drop a perpendicular from the center
lehigh-2020-08.body:
Let $O$ be the center and $M$ the midpoint of $AB$. Then $OM\perp AB$, $MB=12$, so $OM=\sqrt{15^2-12^2}=9$. Since $C$ is on ray $AB$ beyond $B$, $MC=12+28=40$. Therefore $OC=\sqrt{9^2+40^2}=41$.

**Answer: 41**

lehigh-2020-08.title: Power of a point
lehigh-2020-08.body:
Since $C$ is outside, $CA\cdot CB=CO^2-15^2$. Here $CB=28$, $CA=52$, so $CO^2=28\cdot52+225=1456+225=1681=41^2$.

**Answer: 41**

lehigh-2020-09.title: Prime factorization
lehigh-2020-09.body:
$16000=2^7\cdot5^3$. The factor $5$ can only come from digit $5$, so three digits are $5$. The $2^7$ must come from digits $2,4,8$ (any $6$ or other digit would bring in a $3$ or $7$). Each digit contributes at most $2^3$, so at least three digits are needed: $8,8,2$ ($2^3\cdot2^3\cdot2$). That is $6$ digits, the fewest possible (any extra digit $1$ would only lengthen the number). Arranged in increasing order: $255588$.

**Answer: 255588**

lehigh-2020-10.title: Distances from the origin
lehigh-2020-10.body:
$x^2+y^2$ is the squared distance from the origin $O$ to a point $P=(x,y)$ on the circle of radius $14$ centered at $C=(5,12)$. Since $OC=13$, the triangle inequality gives $14=CP\le CO+OP=13+OP$, so $OP\ge1$. Equality occurs when $P$ lies on line $OC$ on the same side of $C$ as $O$ (at distance $14$ from $C$; this point is at distance $1$ from $O$). So the minimum of $x^2+y^2$ is $1$.

**Answer: 1**

lehigh-2020-11.title: Cut off a parallelogram
lehigh-2020-11.body:
Draw through $D$ the line parallel to $AB$ meeting $BC$ at $E$. Then $ABED$ is a parallelogram, so $BE=2$, $DE=6$, and $EC=6$. Triangle $DEC$ has sides $6,6,4$, so by Heron ($s=8$) its area is $\sqrt{8\cdot2\cdot2\cdot4}=8\sqrt2$. Its height from $D$ is $h=\frac{2\cdot8\sqrt2}6=\frac{8\sqrt2}3$, which is also the height of the trapezoid. Area $=\frac{2+8}2\cdot h=\frac{40\sqrt2}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{40\sqrt2}3$**

lehigh-2020-11.title: Compute the height with projections
lehigh-2020-11.body:
Let $x$ be the projection of $DC$ onto $BC$ and $h$ the height. The projection of $AB$ is then $6-x$ (the bases differ by $6$). So $h^2=4^2-x^2=6^2-(6-x)^2=12x-x^2$, giving $16=12x$, $x=\frac43$ and $h=\sqrt{16-\frac{16}9}=\frac{8\sqrt2}3$. Area $=5h=\frac{40\sqrt2}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{40\sqrt2}3$**

lehigh-2020-12.title: Find the ratio from the totals
lehigh-2020-12.body:
Let there have been $B$ boys and $G$ girls. Then $1.2B+1.3G=1.22(B+G)$, so $0.08G=0.02B$ and $B=4G$. This year: boys $4.8G$, girls $1.3G$. The fraction of girls is $\frac{1.3}{6.1}=\frac{13}{61}$.

**Answer: $\frac{13}{61}$**

lehigh-2020-13.title: Evaluate p at -1
lehigh-2020-13.body:
$p(x)=20\prod(x-r_i)$, so $p(-1)=20\prod(-1-r_i)=20\prod(r_i+1)$ (four sign changes). Hence the product is $\frac{p(-1)}{20}=\frac{20-13+11+16}{20}=\frac{34}{20}=1.7$.

**Answer: 1.7**

lehigh-2020-14.title: Split by residue mod 5
Table of small values
lehigh-2020-14.body:
For $n=1,\dots,8$ the values of $\lfloor n^2/5\rfloor$ are $0,0,1,3,5,7,9,12$, giving primes at $n=4,5,6$. For $n\ge7$ the factorizations in the first approach show that the value is never prime.

**Answer: $n=4,5,6$**

lehigh-2020-15.title: Subtract two triangles
lehigh-2020-15.body:
Let the side be $s$. Triangles $AEF$ and $CBF$ are similar with ratio $AE:CB=1:2$, so $AF:FC=1:2$ and the distance from $F$ to $BC$ is $\frac23s$. Hence $[CBF]=\frac12\cdot s\cdot\frac23s=\frac{s^2}3$. Also $[ABE]=\frac12\cdot s\cdot\frac s2=\frac{s^2}4$. Triangles $CBF$ and $ABE$ do not overlap, and what remains of the square is $CDEF$, so its area is $s^2\left(1-\frac13-\frac14\right)=\frac5{12}s^2$.

**Answer: $\frac5{12}$**

lehigh-2020-15.title: Coordinates
lehigh-2020-15.body:
Take $A=(0,0)$, $B=(1,0)$, $C=(1,1)$, $D=(0,1)$, $E=(0,\frac12)$. Line $BE$: $y=\frac12-\frac x2$; line $AC$: $y=x$. They meet at $F=(\frac13,\frac13)$. The shoelace formula for $C,D,E,F$ gives $\frac12\left|(1\cdot1-0\cdot1)+(0\cdot\tfrac12-0\cdot1)+(0\cdot\tfrac13-\tfrac13\cdot\tfrac12)+(\tfrac13\cdot1-1\cdot\tfrac13)\right|=\frac12\left(1-\frac16\right)=\frac5{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac5{12}$**

lehigh-2020-16.title: Factor the sum
lehigh-2020-16.body:
The integers with no prime factor above $3$ are exactly $2^i3^j$ with $i,j\ge0$, each exactly once. So the sum is $\sum_{i,j\ge0}\frac1{2^i3^j}=\left(\sum_i\frac1{2^i}\right)\left(\sum_j\frac1{3^j}\right)=2\cdot\frac32=3$ (all terms are positive so rearranging is allowed).

**Answer: 3**

lehigh-2020-17.title: Count colorings of a 6-cycle
lehigh-2020-17.body:
The six triangles around the center form a cycle $1-2-3-4-5-6-1$ (each triangle shares an edge with its two neighbours; triangles touching only at the center are not adjacent). The number of proper colorings of a cycle $C_n$ with $k$ colors is $(k-1)^n+(-1)^n(k-1)$. With $k=4$, $n=6$: $3^6+3=729+3=732$.

**Answer: 732**

lehigh-2020-17.title: Case on the colors of 1, 3, 5
lehigh-2020-17.body:
Color everything except triangle $4$: $4\cdot3^4=324$ ways (a path $5,6,1,2,3$ of five triangles). Triangle $4$ must differ from $3$ and $5$. If $3$ and $5$ have the same color there are $3$ choices for $4$; otherwise $2$. Colorings of the path with colors of $3$ and $5$ equal: $1,3,5$ all the same color $4\cdot3^2=36$; or $3,5$ equal and different from $1$: $4\cdot3\cdot2^2=48$. Total $84$, giving $84\cdot3=252$; the other $324-84=240$ give $240\cdot2=480$. Sum $=732$.

**Answer: 732**

lehigh-2020-18.title: Factor
lehigh-2020-18.body:
Clearing denominators: $24b+24a=ab$, i.e. $(a-24)(b-24)=576=2^6\cdot3^2$. The number of positive divisors of $576$ is $7\cdot3=21$, so there are $42$ divisors $x$ (positive or negative), and $a=x+24$, $b=24+\frac{576}x$. We need $a,b\ne0$: $a=0$ only for $x=-24$ (then $b=0$ too). All other $41$ divisors give valid pairs.

**Answer: 41**

lehigh-2020-19.title: Which digits can appear
lehigh-2020-19.body:
The first four digits are distinct and their sum is a single digit, at most $9$. Four distinct digits have sum at least $0+1+2+3=6$, so a $0$ must be among them, and it cannot be the first digit. The other three digits are distinct and nonzero with sum at most $9$: $\{1,2,3\},\{1,2,4\},\{1,2,5\},\{1,2,6\},\{1,3,4\},\{1,3,5\},\{2,3,4\}$ ($7$ sets). In each case the last digit (the sum $6,7,8,9,8,9,9$) is not among the first four, so the digits are distinct. For each set the first four digits can be arranged with $0$ not first: $3$ choices for the first digit, $3$ for the second, $2$ for the third, $1$ for the fourth, i.e. $18$ ways. Total $7\cdot18=126$.

**Answer: 126**

lehigh-2020-20.title: Count equally likely outcomes
lehigh-2020-20.body:
Each child is one of $14$ equally likely (gender, day) types. Ordered pairs with at least one (Boy, Sunday): $14+14-1=27$. Of these, the ones with two boys: $7+7-1=13$ (at least one of the two boys born on Sunday). So the probability is $\frac{13}{27}$.

**Answer: $\frac{13}{27}$**

lehigh-2020-21.title: Look for an integer inside the interval
lehigh-2020-21.body:
Write $N=m^2+k$ with $k$ an integer. Since $N>m^2$, $k\ge1$, and the condition is $\frac{2m}{2021}+\frac1{2021^2}<k<\frac{2m}{2020}+\frac1{2020^2}$. For $m\le1009$ the right end is below $1$, so no $k\ge1$ fits. For $m=1010$: $\frac{2020}{2021}+\frac1{2021^2}<1<1+\frac1{2020^2}$, so $k=1$ works. Larger $m$ give larger $N$ (all $N$ for $m$ lie between $m^2$ and $(m+1)^2$), so the smallest is $N=1010^2+1=1020101$.

**Answer: 1020101**

lehigh-2020-23.title: Eliminate x
lehigh-2020-23.body:
The equation gives $x^2-4y^2=4$ with $x\pm2y>0$, so $x>0$ and $x=\sqrt{4+4y^2}$. Let $u=x-y>0$. Then $x=y+u$ and $(y+u)^2-4y^2-4=0$, i.e. $3y^2-2uy+4-u^2=0$. A real $y$ exists only if the discriminant is nonnegative: $4u^2-12(4-u^2)\ge0$, so $u^2\ge3$, $u\ge\sqrt3$. Equality holds at $y=\frac u3=\frac{\sqrt3}3$, $x=\frac{4\sqrt3}3$ (check: $x^2-4y^2=\frac{16}3-\frac43=4$ and $x\pm2y>0$).

**Answer: $\sqrt3$**

lehigh-2020-24.title: Probability of being in each square
lehigh-2020-24.body:
Each square is formed by joining the midpoints of the sides of the previous one, so it has half the area. The point lies in the $n$-th square with probability $2^{-(n-1)}$. By linearity of expectation, the average number of squares is $\sum_{n\ge1}2^{-(n-1)}=1+\frac12+\frac14+\cdots=2$.

**Answer: 2**

lehigh-2020-24.title: Probability of exactly k squares
lehigh-2020-24.body:
The four outer triangles are half of the area, so the point lies in exactly $1$ square with probability $\frac12$, exactly $2$ with probability $\frac14$, etc. The average is $\sum k2^{-k}=\left(\frac12+\frac14+\cdots\right)+\left(\frac14+\frac18+\cdots\right)+\cdots=1+\frac12+\frac14+\cdots=2$.

**Answer: 2**

lehigh-2020-25.title: Place the odd numbers
lehigh-2020-25.body:
There are five odd numbers. Each row sum is odd iff the row has an odd number of odd entries ($1$ or $3$); same for columns. With total five odds and three rows each having $1$ or $3$: the only possibility is $3+1+1$, and similarly for columns. So one row is all odd and one column is all odd, and the other cells in the other rows and columns are even: the odd cells form a 'cross' (one full row and one full column): $5$ cells. There are $3\cdot3=9$ such crosses. Each can be filled in $5!\cdot4!$ ways. Probability $=\frac{9\cdot5!\cdot4!}{9!}=\frac{9\cdot120\cdot24}{362880}=\frac1{14}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{14}$**

lehigh-2020-25.title: Positions of odd numbers only
lehigh-2020-25.body:
Only the pattern of odd/even positions matters: all $\binom95=126$ choices of the five cells for the odd numbers are equally likely. The good ones are the $9$ crosses, so the probability is $\frac9{126}=\frac1{14}$.

**Answer: $\frac1{14}$**

lehigh-2020-26.title: Coordinates
lehigh-2020-26.body:
Put $A=(0,0)$, $B=(s,0)$, $C=(s,s)$, $P=(x,y)$. Then $x^2+y^2=25$, $(x-s)^2+y^2=8$, $(x-s)^2+(y-s)^2=9$. Subtracting the first two gives $2sx-s^2=17$, so $x=\frac{s^2+17}{2s}$. Subtracting the last two gives $(y-s)^2-y^2=1$, so $y=\frac{s^2-1}{2s}$. Substituting into $x^2+y^2=25$: $(s^2+17)^2+(s^2-1)^2=100s^2$, i.e. $2s^4-68s^2+290=0$, $s^4-34s^2+145=0$, so $s^2=5$ or $29$. Because $P$ is inside, $AP\le AC=s\sqrt2$ gives $s^2\ge12.5$, which excludes $5$. So $s^2=29$ (then $x=\frac{46}{2\sqrt{29}}\approx4.27$, $y=\frac{28}{2\sqrt{29}}\approx2.60$, inside the square).

**Answer: 29**

lehigh-2020-27.title: Which counts are possible
lehigh-2020-27.body:
A step raises the count by $n^2-1$. If $3\nmid n$ then $3\mid n^2-1$; if $3\mid n$ then $n^2-1\equiv2\pmod 3$ and $n^2-1\ge8$, so $n^2-1=8+3j$. In both cases $n^2-1$ is a nonnegative combination of $3$ and $8$, and the steps $n=2$ and $n=3$ add exactly $3$ and $8$. So the achievable counts are exactly $1+3k+8\ell$ with $k,\ell\ge0$. Now $m=3k+8\ell$ is representable iff: $m\equiv0\pmod3$ (any $m\ge0$); $m\equiv2$ and $m\ge8$; $m\equiv1$ and $m\ge16$. The non-representable $m$ are $1,4,7,10,13$ and $2,5$, so the unreachable counts $N=m+1$ are $2,3,5,6,8,11,14$, with sum $49$.

**Answer: 49**

lehigh-2020-28.title: Bound and example
lehigh-2020-28.body:
$7531\cdot8=60248$ has distinct even digits, so $7531$ works. A number $x>7531$ with distinct odd digits contains the digit $9$ (without a $9$ the largest is $7531$) and $x\ge7539$. The multiplier $y$ must be even (the product is even, $x$ is odd) and $y\ne10$. A number with distinct even digits has at most five digits and is at most $86420$. If $y\ge12$, then $xy\ge7539\cdot12>86420$. For $y\in\{2,4,6,8\}$, $xy\le86420$ forces $x\le43210$, so $x$ has four digits ($7539\le x\le9753$) or five digits ($x\ge13579$ and $y\le6$). An exhaustive check of these finitely many cases (done by computer) finds no product with distinct even digits (the carry from the digit $9$ always produces an odd digit). So $7531$ is the largest.

**Answer: 7531**

lehigh-2020-29.title: Compare path pairs
lehigh-2020-29.body:
Every path that reaches the forward end first (at position $+8$ before $-8$) has $k+8$ forward and $k$ backward steps, probability $(\frac23)^{k+8}(\frac13)^k$. Swapping F and B gives a path that reaches the backward end first with probability $(\frac13)^{k+8}(\frac23)^k$, and this is a bijection between the two kinds of paths. The ratio of probabilities is $2^8:1$ for each pair. So $P(\text{forward first})=\frac{256}{257}$.

**Answer: $\frac{256}{257}$**

lehigh-2020-29.title: Gambler's ruin
lehigh-2020-29.body:
For a walk with up-probability $p=\frac23$, down $q=\frac13$, starting $8$ from the bottom of a rope of length $16$, the probability to reach the top first is $\frac{1-(q/p)^8}{1-(q/p)^{16}}=\frac{1}{1+(q/p)^8}=\frac1{1+2^{-8}}=\frac{256}{257}$.

**Answer: $\frac{256}{257}$**

lehigh-2020-31.title: Distance between tangent spheres
lehigh-2020-31.body:
Two spheres of radii $r_1,r_2$ tangent to the plane at points a distance $d$ apart and tangent to each other have centers at distance $r_1+r_2$ and vertical offset $|r_1-r_2|$, so $(r_1+r_2)^2=(r_1-r_2)^2+d^2$, i.e. $d^2=4r_1r_2$. With radii $r_A,r_B,r_C$ at the vertices opposite sides $a,b,c$: $r_Ar_B=\frac{c^2}4=\frac{25}4$, $r_Br_C=\frac{a^2}4=\frac94$, $r_Ar_C=\frac{b^2}4=4$ (taking $a=3,b=4,c=5$). Then $r_A^2=\frac{(25/4)\cdot4}{9/4}=\frac{100}9$, so $r_A=\frac{10}3$, $r_B=\frac{25/4}{10/3}=\frac{15}8$, $r_C=\frac{4}{10/3}=\frac65$. The largest is $\frac{10}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{10}3$**

lehigh-2020-32.title: Six circular arcs
lehigh-2020-32.body:
At each stage the hexagon rotates by $60^\circ=\frac\pi3$ about a vertex on the line, and $P$ moves along an arc of that angle about the pivot. The distances from $P$ to the successive pivots are $1,\sqrt3,2,\sqrt3,1,0$ (adjacent vertex, vertex two steps away, opposite vertex, and back). In the last stage $P$ itself is the pivot and does not move. Total length $=\frac\pi3(1+\sqrt3+2+\sqrt3+1)=\frac\pi3(4+2\sqrt3)=\frac{2\pi}3(2+\sqrt3)$.

**Answer: $\frac{2\pi}3(2+\sqrt3)$**

lehigh-2020-33.title: Count by stars and bars
lehigh-2020-33.body:
The number of integers with at most $d$ digits (leading zeros allowed) and digit sum $7$ is the number of solutions of $x_1+\dots+x_d=7$ in nonnegative integers, namely $\binom{d+6}{7}$ (each $x_i\le7<10$ automatically). For $d=3$ this is $\binom97=36$, so there are $36$ such integers below $1000$, and $1006$, the smallest four-digit one, is $a_{37}$. So $n=37$ and $9n=333$. For $d=5$ there are $\binom{11}7=330$ such integers below $100000$, so $a_{331},a_{332},a_{333}$ are the three smallest six-digit ones: $100006$, $100015$, $100024$. Hence $a_{333}=100024$.

**Answer: 100024**

lehigh-2020-34.title: Coupon collector
lehigh-2020-34.body:
After $i-1$ distinct days have been named, each new person names a new day with probability $\frac{7-(i-1)}7$, so the expected waiting time for the $i$th new day is $\frac7{7-i+1}$. Total: $7\left(1+\frac12+\dots+\frac17\right)=1+\frac76+\frac75+\frac74+\frac73+\frac72+7=\frac{363}{20}=18.15$.

**Answer: 18.15**

lehigh-2020-35.title: Functional relation
lehigh-2020-35.body:
$q\!\left(\frac1{1-x}\right)=\dfrac{p(1/(1-x))}{\frac1{1-x}\cdot\frac{-x}{1-x}}=-\frac{(1-x)^2}{x}\,p\!\left(\frac1{1-x}\right)$. Equating with $q(x)$ gives $p(x)=-(1-x)^3\,p\!\left(\frac1{1-x}\right)$. If $p=\sum c_ix^i$ had degree $d\ge4$, the right side would contain the terms $c_i(1-x)^{3-i}$ for $i\ge4$, whose most negative power $(1-x)^{3-d}$ cannot be cancelled, contradicting that the left side is a polynomial. So $\deg p\le3$. Write $p=ax^3+bx^2+cx+d$; the relation gives $a=d$ and $b=-c-3d$. The conditions $p(2)=5$, $p(3)=5$ become $5=-3a-2c$ and $5=a-6c$, so $a=c=-1$, $b=4$, $d=-1$: $p(x)=-x^3+4x^2-x-1$. Therefore $p(4)=-64+64-4-1=-5$. (Check: $p(2)=5$, $p(3)=5$.)

**Answer: -5**

lehigh-2020-36.title: Substitute
lehigh-2020-36.body:
From the first condition $x=k\sin\theta$, $y=k\cos\theta$ for some $k$. The second becomes $\frac{\cos^4\theta}{\sin^4\theta}+\frac{\sin^4\theta}{\cos^4\theta}=\frac{14\sin\theta\cos\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta(\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta)}=14$ (using $x^3y+xy^3=xy(x^2+y^2)=k^4\sin\theta\cos\theta$ and $\sin 2\theta=2\sin\theta\cos\theta$). Let $t=\frac xy=\tan\theta$ and $S=t+\frac1t$. Then $t^4+t^{-4}=14$, and $t^2+t^{-2}=S^2-2$, so $(S^2-2)^2-2=14$, $S^2-2=4$, $S^2=6$. Since $x,y>0$, $S=\sqrt6$.

**Answer: $\sqrt6$**

lehigh-2020-38.title: Generating functions
lehigh-2020-38.body:
The generating functions of allowed values are $\frac x{1-x^2}$ for $a_1$, $\frac{x(1-x^2)}{(1-x)(1-x^3)}$ for $a_2$ (all positive integers minus multiples of $3$: $\frac x{1-x}-\frac{x^3}{1-x^3}$) and $\frac{x(1-x^3)}{(1-x)(1-x^4)}$ for $a_3$. Their product is $\frac{x^3}{(1-x)^2(1-x^4)}$. We need the coefficient of $x^{2020}$, i.e. of $x^{2017}$ in $(1+2x+3x^2+\cdots)(1+x^4+x^8+\cdots)$. It equals $\sum_{j=0}^{504}(2018-4j)=505\cdot2018-4\cdot\frac{504\cdot505}2=505\cdot1010=510050$.

**Answer: 510050**

lehigh-2020-39.title: Radii ratio and an infinite product
lehigh-2020-39.body:
A regular $m$-gon circumscribed about a circle of radius $r$ has circumradius $\frac r{\cos(\pi/m)}$. Since $P_{n-1}$ has $2^n$ sides, $r_n=\frac{r_{n-1}}{\cos(\pi/2^n)}$, so $r_n=\prod_{k=2}^n\frac1{\cos(\pi/2^k)}$. By the double-angle formula, $\sin x=2^n\sin\frac x{2^n}\prod_{k=1}^n\cos\frac x{2^k}$, so $\frac{\sin x}x=\prod_{k\ge1}\cos\frac x{2^k}$. For $x=\frac\pi2$: $\frac2\pi=\prod_{k\ge1}\cos\frac\pi{2^{k+1}}=\prod_{k\ge2}\cos\frac\pi{2^k}$. Hence $\lim r_n=\frac\pi2$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2$**

lehigh-2020-40.title: Equal inradii
lehigh-2020-40.body:
Let $x=BD$, $y=CD$. For a triangle, area $=r\cdot$ semiperimeter, so with equal inradii $\frac{[ACD]}{[BCD]}=\frac{\text{perimeter}(ACD)}{\text{perimeter}(BCD)}=\frac{6-x+y}{1+x+y}$. On the other hand the two triangles have the same height from $C$, so the ratio is $\frac{AD}{BD}=\frac{3-x}x$. Equating gives $y=\frac{4x-3}{3-2x}$. The law of cosines in $BCD$ ($\cos B=\frac16$) gives $y^2=x^2+1-\frac x3$. Substituting, $12x^4-40x^3+3x^2+27x=0$, i.e. $x(x-3)(12x^2-4x-9)=0$, so $x=\frac{1+2\sqrt7}6$ (the root in $(0,3)$), and then $y=\frac{\sqrt7}2$. The area of $ABC$ is $\frac12\cdot1\cdot\sqrt{9-\frac14}=\frac{\sqrt{35}}4$, and it equals $r$ times the sum of the two semiperimeters, $r\cdot\frac{(6-x+y)+(1+x+y)}2=r\cdot\frac{7+2y}2=r\cdot\frac{7+\sqrt7}2$. Hence $r=\frac{\sqrt{35}}{2(7+\sqrt7)}=\frac{\sqrt{35}(7-\sqrt7)}{84}=\frac{7\sqrt{35}-7\sqrt5}{84}=\frac{\sqrt{35}-\sqrt5}{12}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt{35}-\sqrt5}{12}$**
